comments.text:
The caffeine thing got me and I'm gonna talk about it for a minute; I'm from Quebec, and a bill was passed this year that will take effect December 11th banning energy drinks to those under 16. The impetus for this was the death of a 15 year old who drank (according to the story) 1 can of redbull, that negatively interacted with his ADHD medication (which is in most circumstances a stimulant, contrary to popular belief). People have been demonizing caffeine since before then though, and the focus on that specifically is often ridiculous. For an otherwise healthy human being it is physically impossible to drink enough caffeinated beverage to actually reach the overdose threshold (which is something like 10000mg). For one thing your body can't process more than about a liter of liquid per hour, and for another caffeine has a half-life in the body of a few hours, so you'd need to get that 10k mg in a few short hours. It's not happening. The documented cases of death directly attributed to caffeine overdose are ALL due to consumption of caffeine pills since that's genuinely the only way to get enough of it into you quickly enough to do damage.

There are other stories like that boy who died, such as a woman who died after drinking a caffeinated lemonade at Panera a few years back, and various others. The commonality they all share is that the people who died had severe health issues and/or were on some pretty serious medication and should absolutely have been aware of the potential negative interaction caffeine would have. Demonizing caffeine rather making any attempt to educate people is an insane reaction that doesn't help anybody. Not least of which due to the fact that caffeine is present in things like coffee and tea, both of which are (and this is true) not energy drinks, and thus are readily available all day every day for anybody who wants to buy them. This ban in Quebec targets energy drinks specifically, and we already have a limit in Canada of 170mg of caffeine in such drinks.....a limit that doesn't apply to delicious cans of Starbucks Triple Shot, as they have almost double the amount a similar sized energy drink has. I'm not saying anybody dying from a drink is a good thing, but I'm saying people need to be more aware of their own health conditions and absolutely should be aware of what the medication they're on might actually react with in some negative way.
